land.text: 'Gandhara proper': the Peshawar valley west of the Indus, which Cyrus annexed 'around 535 BCE' (the Gandhara dossier, sa-01-a, loses it in -535)

predecessors.note: The infobox of the Gandara page says 'Preceded by: Gandhara'.

land.text: 'In 327 BCE, Alexander the Great conquered Gandhara'; Oxyartes named satrap in 326

successors.note: The infobox dates the end to 'August/September c. 330 BCE' (after Gaugamela) and lists the local kingdoms of Taxiles, Peucelaotis, Abisares and Assacani as successors; Cliopatria keeps its Achaemenid row to 327, so the end here is the text's 327. Those kingdoms have no dossier.

capitals.name: Pushkalavati (Charsadda)
capitals.note: 'The satrapy's capital was Pushkalavati, present-day Charsadda', centre of Peucelaotis 'ruled by an indigenous family under the Achaemenids'; Astes, the last known satrap, died in the siege of Peucelaotis (Gandara page; undated). Coordinates are the town's (the page gives none).

correction.text: 'Gandhara included the entire Peshawar Valley' (conquest page) with its capital Pushkalavati (Charsadda), and 'its western portion was called Paropamisadae' in the Behistun versions (the Kabul valley); Taxila, which the pages put in Hindush, is left out

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Gandara row; the Achaemenid Empire row draws 132 of the 193 cells of the Gandhara region in -350 and the same western part from -540). The page gives no area; the shape resolves to about 59,000 km2. The page names the Peshawar valley, the capital and the Kabul-side Paropamisadae, not a boundary; 'Sethna held that Cyrus conquered only the trans-Indus borderlands around Peshawar', so the eastern edge is the Indus.

region.text: 'Gandhara included the entire Peshawar Valley' (conquest page) with its capital Pushkalavati (Charsadda), and 'its western portion was called Paropamisadae' in the Behistun versions (the Kabul valley); Taxila, which the pages put in Hindush, is left out

ledger.note: c. 535 BCE: Cyrus makes Gandhara a Persian satrapy. 'Around 535 BCE' the Persian king 'organized the conquered territories under the Satrapy of Gandara'; the Gandara page's infobox has 'Cyrus II (c. 535-530 BCE)' as first ruler and its text 'by the later 6th century BCE'; the 518 BCE of other pages is the Behistun date, when Gandara is listed among Darius's provinces.

region.text: 'Gandhara included the entire Peshawar Valley' (conquest page) with its capital Pushkalavati (Charsadda), and 'its western portion was called Paropamisadae' in the Behistun versions (the Kabul valley); Taxila, which the pages put in Hindush, is left out

ledger.note: 327 BCE: Alexander conquers Gandhara. 'He conquered Gandhara in 327 BCE', invited the Indus Valley chieftains to submit that winter and fought the Assakenoi in April 326; Oxyartes is named satrap in 326. The infobox says 'Disestablished: August/September c. 330 BCE' and the local kingdoms of Taxiles, Peucelaotis, Abisares and Assacani as successors; the Indian-campaign page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_campaign_of_Alexander_the_Great) has the campaign from 'the end of the spring of 327 BC'.

wars.name: Achaemenid conquest of the Indus Valley

zones.text: the Peshawar valley and Taxila country

wars.outcome: Persian victory: 'Cyrus probably went as far as the banks of the Indus river' and 'organized the conquered territories under the Satrapy of Gandara'; the push to the Jhelum came 'around 518 BCE'.
wars.note: Infobox 'c. 535/518 BCE - 323 BCE'. The Hindush dossier carries the southern half of the same war.

wars.name: Indian campaign of Alexander the Great

zones.text: the Swat valley, where 'the Assakenoi lived', and Peucelaotis

wars.outcome: Macedonian victory: Gandhara conquered in 327, the Assakenoi 'of Massaga fought him under the command of their queen, Cleophis' and were reduced by stratagem; Alexander 'annexes northwestern India'.
wars.note: The Asvaka page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A%C5%9Bvaka) gives the Swat valley and the war 'which began in 327 BCE' with losses at Beira, Massaga and Ora; no dates for the sieges. The Indian-campaign page dates Aornos to April 326 BC. Trimmed by the reviewer (2026-10-18) to -327 ('In 327 BCE, Alexander the Great conquered Gandhara', Gandara page), the dossier's end year; the Assakenoi sieges of 326 fall after the satrapy's end and belong to macedonian-empire.

certainty.note: The satrapy is known from inscriptions and Greek authors, not from boundaries; the Indus edge, the Kabul edge and the Taxila line are approximate.

sources.title: Gandara

notes: Type colony (satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire, family persia): the Iran group's Achaemenid dossier should carry the matching relation; Cliopatria's Achaemenid row already draws about two thirds of the Peshawar valley region to 327 and the Kabul valley. Dates: -535 is the conquest page's 'around 535 BCE'; the Gandara page's infobox puts the satrapy's establishment in 518 (and a 500 BCE conquest) in the infobox only; the end -327 is the text's, the infobox's c. 330 is the end of Persian royal authority. Between 330 and 327 the Gandara infobox lists four local successor kingdoms (Taxiles, Peucelaotis, Abisares, Assacani); none has a dossier and none held land for ten years on these pages. Overlap: the Hindush dossier takes Taxila (100 km) because the same page calls Ambhi 'ruler of Taxila in the former Hindush satrapy' and the conquest page makes Taxila Hindush's capital; the Gandara infobox lists the Kingdom of Taxiles as Gandara's successor, so the pages disagree and the Taxila line is soft. The Kashmir valley, held back by the Gandhara kingdom in -535 (sa-01-a), is in neither dossier. Gazetteer: Charsadda/Pushkalavati (34.20N 71.74E) is not a place; Mardan and Saidu (Swat) stand in for the sieges' country.
